title: The ticket you cannot afford to skip: inside Spain's Christmas lottery

words.zh: 承担不起（做某事的后果）；买不起
words.note: afford 本义是“买得起”。cannot afford to do 还常表示“不能冒险去……”：We cannot afford to wait.（我们等不起。）
words.ctx: The ticket you cannot afford to skip: inside Spain's Christmas lottery

ex.en: We [[cannot afford to]] lose this customer.
ex.zh: 我们丢不起这个客户。

ex.en: I [[can't afford to]] take a taxi every day.
ex.zh: 我可没钱天天打车。

words.def: to not have enough money to buy something; to be unable to risk something happening

cf.diff: can't afford sth 是“买不起”；can't afford to do 还可以指“承担不起做某事的后果”（We can't afford to wait.）。

ex.en: We [[can't afford to]] lose this customer.
ex.zh: 我们可丢不起这个客户。

cloze.before: The ticket you cannot

words.note: skip breakfast（不吃早饭）、skip a class（逃一节课）、skip the ads（跳过广告）。
words.ctx: The ticket you cannot afford to skip: inside Spain's Christmas lottery

ex.en: Don't [[skip]] breakfast before an exam.
ex.zh: 考试前别不吃早饭。

words.def: to not do or attend something you usually do; to leave something out

cf.diff: skip 是“故意不做、跳过”（skip breakfast 不吃早饭）；miss 多是“错过”，可能并非故意（miss the bus）。

ex.en: I [[missed]] the last train.
ex.zh: 我没赶上末班车。

words.zh: 入股、合买；（比喻）相信、认同
words.note: buy into a business（入股生意）。比喻：I don't buy into that idea.（我不信那一套。）
words.ctx: Every December, millions of Spaniards buy into the same few numbers, hoping for the prize they call El Gordo, the Fat One.

ex.en: Five friends [[bought into]] the same ticket.
ex.zh: 五个朋友合买了同一张彩票。

ex.en: I don't [[buy into]] all that hype.
ex.zh: 我不信那些炒作。

words.def: to pay for a share of something; to believe in an idea

words.note: leave sb out（把某人排除在外），feel left out（感到被冷落）。
words.ctx: Few expect to win; what they really fear is being left out.

words.note: date back to + 时间 / date back + 一段时间：The church dates back to 1200.（这座教堂建于 1200 年。）也说 date from。

ex.en: The castle [[dates back]] to the 12th century.
ex.zh: 这座城堡可追溯到 12 世纪。

ex.en: Their friendship [[dates back]] to school.
ex.zh: 他们的友谊从上学时就开始了。

words.def: to have existed since a particular time in the past

words.note: 容易认出来的特点：a distinctive voice / smell / style。名词 distinction。

ex.zh: 她的笑声很有特点。

ex.en: The building's [[distinctive]] red roof is easy to spot.
ex.zh: 这栋楼独特的红屋顶很好认。

words.def: having a quality that makes something easy to recognize and different from others

words.note: a fraction of the cost（成本的一小部分），in a fraction of a second（一瞬间）。数学里的“分数”也是 fraction。
words.ctx: Full tickets are expensive, so most people buy a fraction of one, known as a décimo, a tenth.

ex.zh: 价格只是原价的零头。

ex.en: Only a [[fraction]] of the guests stayed late.
ex.zh: 只有少数客人待到很晚。

words.def: a small part or amount of something; a number such as ½

words.note: 比之前做得更多：Some go further and ...（有些人更进一步……）。
words.ctx: Many go further and split tickets with colleagues, neighbours, the local bar or the football club.

ex.en: Some schools [[go further]] and ban phones completely.
ex.zh: 有些学校更进一步，完全禁止带手机。

ex.en: She [[went further]] and quit her job.
ex.zh: 她更进一步，直接辞了职。

words.def: to do more or go to a greater degree than others

cloze.before: Many go

cloze.szh: 很多人更进一步，和同事、邻居、街角酒吧或足球俱乐部一起分摊彩票。

ex.zh: 全班分成了三组。

words.def: to divide something into parts and share it

words.note: My number came up!（我的号码中了！）也常指话题出现：Your name came up in the meeting.

ex.zh: 那位部长被迫辞职。

words.note: 强调两件事几乎同时发生。No sooner 放句首时后面倒装：No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.（我刚坐下电话就响了。）注意后半句用 than，不用 when。
words.ctx: No sooner has the last prize been sung than winners in lucky towns are spraying each other with sparkling wine on national television.

ex.en: [[No sooner]] had we arrived than it started to rain.
ex.zh: 我们刚到就下起了雨。

ex.en: [[No sooner]] had she left than he called.
ex.zh: 她刚走他就打来了电话。

words.conn: No sooner + had / has + 主语 + 过去分词 ... than + 句子

pick.q: No sooner ___ home than the power went out.
pick.why: No sooner 放句首要倒装，助动词 had 提到主语 I 前面。

pick.q: No sooner had the film started ___ the baby began to cry.
pick.why: No sooner 固定和 than 搭配；hardly / scarcely 才和 when 搭配。

ex.zh: 农民春天给庄稼喷药。

words.def: to cover something with small drops of liquid

cloze.before: No sooner has the last prize been sung than winners in lucky towns are
cloze.after: each other with sparkling wine on national television.
cloze.szh: 最后一个奖刚唱完，幸运小镇里的中奖者就已经在全国电视直播中互相喷起起泡酒来了。

words.note: 挂在墙上或街上的长条布：a banner reading "Welcome"。网页上的“横幅广告”也叫 banner。
words.ctx: Shops that sold the winning number hang banners boasting of their luck, and the queues outside them grow longer the following year.

ex.en: Fans held up a huge [[banner]].
ex.zh: 球迷举起了一条巨大的横幅。

ex.en: A [[banner]] across the street announced the festival.
ex.zh: 街上挂着一条横幅宣布节日。

words.def: a long piece of cloth with words on it, carried or hung up for people to see

cloze.before: Shops that sold the winning number hang
cloze.after: boasting of their luck, and the queues outside them grow longer the following year.
cloze.szh: 卖出中奖号码的彩票店会挂出横幅炫耀自己的好运，第二年店门外的队伍也会排得更长。

words.note: boast of / about sth。也可以表示（地方）拥有值得骄傲的东西：The city boasts two universities.
words.ctx: Shops that sold the winning number hang banners boasting of their luck, and the queues outside them grow longer the following year.

ex.en: He likes to [[boast about]] his car.
ex.zh: 他喜欢炫耀他的车。

ex.en: The hotel [[boasts of]] a fine view.
ex.zh: 这家酒店以美景自豪。

words.def: to talk with too much pride about something you have or have done

cf.diff: boast 多指用嘴“吹嘘”；show off 也可以是拿东西出来“显摆”。

cloze.before: Shops that sold the winning number hang banners
cloze.after: of their luck, and the queues outside them grow longer the following year.

words.note: 形容词 superstitious（迷信的）。Breaking a mirror brings bad luck is an old superstition.
words.ctx: Superstition plays its part, too.

ex.en: It's just a [[superstition]].
ex.zh: 那只是迷信。

ex.en: Many sports fans have little [[superstitions]].
ex.zh: 很多球迷都有些小迷信。

words.def: a belief that certain objects or actions bring good or bad luck

cloze.after: plays its part, too.
cloze.szh: 迷信也起了作用。

words.note: play a part in sth：在……中起作用。Everyone has to play their part.（每个人都要尽一份力。）
words.ctx: Superstition plays its part, too.

ex.en: Luck [[played its part]], too.
ex.zh: 运气也起了作用。

ex.en: Everyone must [[play their part]].
ex.zh: 每个人都要尽一份力。

words.def: to do your share of the work in something

words.zh: 销售点、门店；（情绪的）发泄途径
words.note: retail outlet（零售店），fast-food outlet（快餐店）。also：an outlet for stress（释放压力的途径）。
words.ctx: People travel across the country to buy from outlets with a lucky reputation, and some rub their tickets on a pregnant friend's belly for luck.

ex.en: The chain has 200 [[outlets]] across the country.
ex.zh: 这家连锁店在全国有 200 家门店。

ex.en: Music is my [[outlet]] for stress.
ex.zh: 音乐是我释放压力的方式。

words.def: a shop or place that sells a company's products; a way of expressing strong feelings

cloze.before: People travel across the country to buy from
cloze.after: with a lucky reputation, and some rub their tickets on a pregnant friend's belly for luck.
cloze.szh: 人们跨越大半个国家，去有“幸运”名声的彩票点买票，有的人还会把彩票在怀孕朋友的肚子上蹭一蹭，图个好运。

words.note: rub one's eyes（揉眼睛），rub A on B（把 A 在 B 上蹭）。rub it in：揭人伤疤。
words.ctx: People travel across the country to buy from outlets with a lucky reputation, and some rub their tickets on a pregnant friend's belly for luck.

ex.en: He [[rubbed]] his tired eyes.
ex.zh: 他揉了揉疲惫的眼睛。

ex.en: [[Rub]] the cream into your skin.
ex.zh: 把乳霜揉进皮肤里。

words.def: to move your hand or an object backwards and forwards over a surface while pressing it

cloze.before: People travel across the country to buy from outlets with a lucky reputation, and some
cloze.after: their tickets on a pregnant friend's belly for luck.

words.note: For all his money, he isn't happy.（尽管他有钱，却并不快乐。）= despite。
words.ctx: For all the talk of jackpots, the real prize may be the feeling of being in it together.

ex.en: [[For all]] its problems, I love this city.
ex.zh: 尽管有种种问题，我还是爱这座城市。

ex.en: [[For all]] her fame, she lives simply.
ex.zh: 尽管很有名，她生活得很简朴。

words.def: despite something

cf.diff: for all 很口语，常带“尽管有这么多……（却）”的语气；despite / in spite of 是普通的“尽管”。

ex.en: [[Despite]] the rain, we went out.
ex.zh: 尽管下雨，我们还是出去了。

cloze.after: the talk of jackpots, the real prize may be the feeling of being in it together.
cloze.szh: 尽管大家嘴上都在谈大奖，真正的奖品也许是“大家一起”的那种感觉。

words.note: win / hit the jackpot：中大奖；比喻“交好运、发大财”。
words.ctx: For all the talk of jackpots, the real prize may be the feeling of being in it together.

ex.en: She won the [[jackpot]] last week.
ex.zh: 她上周中了头奖。

ex.en: We really hit the [[jackpot]] with this hotel.
ex.zh: 订到这家酒店，我们真是走大运了。

words.def: the biggest prize in a lottery or competition

cf.diff: hit the jackpot 也常用来比喻“突然交好运、大获成功”。

ex.en: We really [[hit the jackpot]] with this flat.
ex.zh: 我们租到这套房子真是走大运了。

cloze.after: , the real prize may be the feeling of being in it together.
cloze.szh: 尽管大家嘴上都在谈大奖，真正的奖品也许是“大家一起”的那种感觉。

words.note: We're all in it together.（我们是一条船上的人。）
words.ctx: For all the talk of jackpots, the real prize may be the feeling of being in it together.

ex.en: Don't worry, we're all [[in it together]].
ex.zh: 别担心，我们是一条船上的。

ex.en: The team felt they were [[in it together]].
ex.zh: 队员们觉得大家是同舟共济的。

words.def: to be in the same difficult situation as other people and face it together

words.note: Getting lost is half the fun.（迷路正是乐趣所在。）表示过程本身就很有意思。
words.ctx: But they will lose together, and that, Spaniards insist, is half the fun.

ex.en: Planning the trip is [[half the fun]].
ex.zh: 计划旅行本身就是乐趣的一半。

ex.en: Getting there is [[half the fun]].
ex.zh: 去的路上就是乐趣所在。

words.def: a large part of the enjoyment of something

cloze.before: But they will lose together, and that, Spaniards insist, is half the
cloze.szh: 但他们会一起输，而西班牙人坚持说，这正是一半的乐趣所在。
